On Tue, Nov 18, 2014 at 1:59 PM, Josh Brindley <joshuab...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dr. Matzke,

I running into an error trying to run your program biogeobears, and I can't seem to find any solutions on the google group. When running the DEC analysis and everything runs fine until I get to the check_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object) where I am getting this error, 

Error in rowSums(tmp_tipranges) : 'x' must be numeric

I have attached my data. Do you have any ideas what could be causing this? Thank you fr taking a look.

Cheers,
Josh


Hi Josh, 

Thanks for the question, this uncovered a case my error checks weren't catching.

The problem was that one of the area names was a duplicate of another in the geography file. You had:

A ENM SW NW B NM SM C S A

As you can see, "A" is used twice. If you change the second A to A2, it works fine.

I'll add an error check in a few spots in the code.

Cheers!
Nick

Hi Josh -- you didn't send your run script, so I don't know if there was something there, but the only things I found in what you sent:

1.  You should have "Af" instead of "A" for the areas_allowed and dispersal_multipliers files, so that the area names in these files match what is in the geography file. I don't know if that would have caused a crash.

2. By chance, your tree has a node at exactly 125 million years ago, and your time-stratification was happening at 125 million years ago. The script threw a stop error indicating this, but perhaps your R setup didn't show the error text. the script doesn't like it because when the tree is being divided up at 125, what should be done with a node exactly on that line?  It's not clear.  Anyway, if you change the timeperiod to 125.1 my it works.

3. Also, I've done some minor updates to the BioGeoBEARS code, one of which fixed an issue that might have come up in time-stratified analysis, so you should make sure run the source() commands again.

It looks like its working...

I'm attaching the inputs and scripts for a 5-areas-max and 10-areas-max run, each of them running on 8 cores on my mac.  If you're on Windows (max cores = 1 I think in R multicore stuff) or have fewer cores, you'll have to change this.

I'm running each analysis now with 8 cores, it will probably take overnight though and might not check it til Monday.

Cheers!
Nick
